initial_prompt: What's the difference between a virus and bacteria?

messages.content: What's the difference between a virus and bacteria?

Viruses and bacteria are fundamentally different types of microorganisms. Bacteria are living cells - they can reproduce on their own, have their own metabolism, and can survive independently. Viruses aren't really "alive" in the traditional sense - they're basically genetic material (DNA or RNA) wrapped in a protein coat that can only reproduce by hijacking living cells.

This is why antibiotics work against bacteria but not viruses - antibiotics target bacterial cell processes that viruses don't have. Bacteria are typically much larger (you can see some under a regular microscope), while viruses are tiny and need an electron microscope.
